title: Comparison by exact kernel invariants
statement: Let A be a finite ring annihilated by ell^s, G a profinite group, B a profinite group in universe zero, and pi:G -> B a continuous surjective homomorphism. Suppose every finite continuous quotient Q of ker(pi) (in the universe of G) has order coprime to ell. For every discrete continuous A[G]-module M, form the actual fixed submodule N=M^ker(pi) with its descended B-action. There is an isomorphism H^q(G,M) ~= H^q(B,N) for every natural q, where H is [def-exc-continuous-cohomology].

proof.text: Define N as the intersection of the kernels of rho(h)-id for h in ker(pi). Normality makes it G-stable and the trivial kernel action descends it to B. The continuous surjection from compact G to Hausdorff B is a quotient map, so each stabilizer in B is open. Equivariant maps restrict to N, defining the kernel-invariants functor T.

For a lift x of a kernel-fixed y, choose an open normal subgroup U of ker(pi) contained in the stabilizer of x. Sum rho(q)x over the finite quotient Q=ker(pi)/U. Left translation permutes the summands, so the sum is fixed; its image is |Q|y. Choose a,b with a|Q|+b ell^s=1, and multiply the sum by a. Since ell^s annihilates all A-modules, this is a fixed lift of y. Use underlying-module detection of exactness to conclude T preserves exact sequences and homology.

Inflation along pi preserves coefficient modules and monomorphisms. Restrict an equivariant map from an inflated module to the fixed submodule, or compose with its inclusion, to give the adjunction inflation left adjoint to T. The adjunction transports injective extension problems and shows T preserves injectives.

The all-invariants submodule of M is naturally linearly equivalent to the B-invariants of T(M), by inclusion of fixed elements in both directions. Use the natural identifications of the invariant functors from the continuous-cochain comparison to obtain a natural isomorphism of these functors. Apply T to an injective resolution: exactness makes its augmentation a quasi-isomorphism, and its terms are injective. Termwise identification of all-invariants now identifies the homology computing both right derived functors.
